summary: Poisson GLM (log link) for motor TPL claim frequency, GLM1 of the Noll/Salzmann/Wuthrich case study. The script reads the OpenML CSV with both double and single quotes as quote characters (strings such as 'D' and 'B12' arrive without quotes), caps ClaimNb at 4 and Exposure at 1, and engineers nine features: AreaGLM (integer code of Area's alphabetical factor levels A..F -> 1..6), VehPowerGLM (factor of pmin(VehPower, 9)), VehAgeGLM (lookup: VehAge 0 -> 1, 1..10 -> 2, 11..110 -> 3; reference 2), DrivAgeGLM (lookup on DrivAge-17: 18-20 -> 1, 21-25 -> 2, 26-30 -> 3, 31-40 -> 4, 41-50 -> 5, 51-70 -> 6, 71-100 -> 7; reference 5), BonusMalusGLM (pmin(BonusMalus, 150)), DensityGLM (log Density), VehBrand (reference B1), Region (reference R24), VehGas (reference Diesel). A random 90/10 split (set.seed(100), sample without replacement) gives learn/test. glm(ClaimNb ~ ..., offset = log(Exposure), family = poisson()) is fitted on learn: 49 coefficients, treatment contrasts, the offset is the log of the CAPPED exposure and is also used by predict(type='response') on newdata. No rows are dropped and there are no missing values.

preprocessing.description: Read the CSV; both " and ' are quote characters, so single-quoted string values (Area, VehBrand, VehGas, Region) lose their quotes. Header names are already syntactic (make.names leaves them unchanged). Keep all 678,013 rows in file order.
Cap exposure at 1 year (this capped value feeds the offset).
Integer code of Area within its sorted factor levels (A=1 .. F=6); numeric term.
Cap VehPower at 9 and make a factor; levels 4..9 (numeric order), reference 4.

preprocessing.r_code: VehAgeGLM <- cbind(c(0:110), c(1, rep(2, 10), rep(3, 100))); dat$VehAgeGLM <- as.factor(VehAgeGLM[dat$VehAge + 1, 2]); dat[, "VehAgeGLM"] <- relevel(dat[, "VehAgeGLM"], ref = "2")
preprocessing.description: Band VehAge: 0 -> 1, 1..10 -> 2, 11..110 -> 3 (row VehAge+1 of the lookup; outside 0..110 would be NA). Factor relevelled so 2 is the reference: levels ['2','1','3'].

preprocessing.r_code: DrivAgeGLM <- cbind(c(18:100), c(rep(1, 3), rep(2, 5), rep(3, 5), rep(4, 10), rep(5, 10), rep(6, 20), rep(7, 30))); dat$DrivAgeGLM <- as.factor(DrivAgeGLM[dat$DrivAge - 17, 2]); relevel(ref = "5")

preprocessing.description: Natural log of Density; numeric term.

preprocessing.r_code: dat$VehBrand <- relevel(as.factor(dat$VehBrand), ref = "B1"); dat$Region <- relevel(as.factor(dat$Region), ref = "R24"); dat$VehGas <- as.factor(dat$VehGas)
preprocessing.description: Factors with references B1, R24 and Diesel; level order as captured in xlevels (string sort, e.g. B1, B10, B11, ..., B2).

preprocessing.r_code: set.seed(100); ll <- sample(c(1:nrow(dat)), round(0.9 * nrow(dat)), replace = FALSE); learn <- dat[ll, ]; test <- dat[-ll, ]
preprocessing.description: Random 90/10 split. Not re-implemented: membership comes from the harness.

model.formula: ClaimNb ~ VehPowerGLM + VehAgeGLM + DrivAgeGLM + BonusMalusGLM + VehBrand + VehGas + DensityGLM + Region + AreaGLM, offset = log(Exposure)

randomness: set.seed(100) then sample() of round(0.9*n) row numbers without replacement (learn); the rest is test. Seeded, but sample()'s algorithm depends on the R version. The harness supplies the captured membership (R-RNG-01).
risks: The offset log(Exposure) is not a formula term and is easy to drop; it must be applied both in fitting and in predict (R-EST-03).
The exposure in the offset is the capped value (pmin(Exposure, 1)).
Lookup-table banding is positional (VehAge+1, DrivAge-17); out-of-range ages would give NA classes in R.
Factor level orders come from relevel(); VehBrand/Region level order is R string sort (B10 before B2) and must be taken from xlevels.
Driver age is a protected characteristic used as a rating factor (GOV-01: migrate faithfully, flag for validation).
The response is capped at 4, which changes the Poisson likelihood for the affected policies.
